result.title: FlowIR: Depth-driven Rectified Flow for Resolving Thermal Ambiguity in Infrared Super-Resolution
result.comment: Accepted to the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Multimedia & Expo (ICME 2026)
result.summary: Distinguishing different heat sources in low-resolution infrared (IR) images is inherently difficult, as multiple thermal emitters often collapse into ambiguous and overlapping responses. Existing super-resolution methods hallucinate structures from such ambiguous 2D evidence, leading to thermal drift, boundary merging, and unreliable restoration under infrared degradations. We propose FlowIR, a depth-driven rectified flow framework that resolves thermal ambiguity by injecting 3D geometric cues into the generation process. Pseudo-3D depth lifting and depth-guided 3D convolutions disentangle overlapping foreground objects, while cluster-wise inter-attention suppresses cross-source feature contamination. A Thermal-Geometry Consistency Loss further enforces geometric alignment during refinement. Built upon a lightweight rectified flow backbone, FlowIR restores IR images in only a few steps, producing sharply separated, degradation-robust, and geometrically faithful high-resolution results.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FlowIR，一种借助伪三维深度提升与深度引导三维卷积的 rectified flow 框架，用于缓解红外超分辨率中热源重叠造成的热歧义。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究目标是用深度几何先验改善红外图像生成质量，不涉及多模态推理状态、证据获取或 latent 视觉推理，且其扩散式生成属于图像复原而非推理轨迹，缺少可供核查的状态或训练线索。
